notes:
Summary: PaceCore is building a millisecond-sensitive recommendation layer for trading signals and customer support routing. Primary constraints: p99 latency and per-request cost targets. Interested in Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization).

Key requirements / callouts:
- Workload: synchronous reranking + short-context chat for support (median request = 220 tokens; typical prompt prefix reused across requests).
- Latency targets: median < 20ms inference, p95 < 35ms, p99 < 60ms at sustained 1.5k QPS for reranking path. For chat path: median < 50ms.
- Throughput: baseline 1.5k QPS with 30% occasional bursts to 3k QPS. Need autoscale/burst behavior guaranteed under SLA.
- Cost sensitivity: target $0.0004 per recommendation (aggressive). Open to quantized model variants if quality loss < 1% MRR impact.
- Perf tooling: wants Redwood perf benchmark (end-to-end) including compiler/kernel selection metrics and token-level cost breakdown. Will provide representative traffic replay + golden eval set for quality regression checks.
- Batching & caching: heavy interest in automatic prefix/KV caching because ~60% of requests share a common prompt prefix. Wants suggested batching window sizes and expected latency trade-offs.
- Quantization: request to run int8 and nf4 candidate trials; must include quality delta on reranking NDCG and chat coherence metrics.
- Routing/fallbacks: require automatic fallback to a smaller/cheaper model when capacity constrained; must preserve output semantics (blacklist certain models).
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS integration, and EU data residency for part of workload. On-prem private control plane preferred for EU-regulated trading desks.

- SE asks for canonical traffic replay; they'll share anonymized request traces by 3/12.
